levels.native: the platform does it with configuration
levels.add-on: one more managed piece (a function, a second service) does it
levels.you build: code you write and run does it

jobs.job: ingest: accept a write from a device and fan it out to listeners
firebase: a write to a path; every onValue listener on that path receives the change
aws: native
MQTT publish into IoT Core; subscribers on the topic receive it
self: native
MQTT publish into the broker; subscribers receive it

jobs.job: latest state per device (status, settings reported), readable on app open
firebase: the path holds the latest value; overwrite is the default
aws: add-on
a rule action writes the message into a DynamoDB table keyed by device (or the Device Shadow at $1.25 per million operations)
self: add-on
a retained message on the broker gives the latest to a new subscriber; a collector keeps it in a table

jobs.job: history: append, range query by device and time, retention
firebase: append works; range queries need .indexOn per path; retention is a scheduled function that deletes old keys, and storage is billed at the database rate
aws: add-on
a rule action into Firehose, batched to S3 (cold), and a second action into DynamoDB with a TTL (hot); the chart reads the hot table
self: add-on
a collector subscribes and inserts into TimescaleDB; a retention policy drops old chunks; compression is a table setting

jobs.job: events: append once (replay-safe), two fields the app may set
firebase: a key the device derives, a .write rule of !data.exists() and two mutable children
aws: add-on
a rule action with a conditional DynamoDB put on the id; the app's acknowledgement goes through the API
self: you build
the collector inserts with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; the acknowledgement is an API the app calls

jobs.job: settings desired / reported with a version the device echoes
firebase: two paths; the device listens to desired and overwrites reported
aws: native
the Device Shadow is exactly desired / reported / delta with a version
self: add-on
a retained settings topic the device subscribes to; reported is a second topic the collector stores

jobs.job: presence: offline after N3's window, judged where silence is observed
firebase: a scheduled function compares each status ts with now; onDisconnect writes exist for SDK clients but not for a REST device
aws: native
the last will on the MQTT session, plus lifecycle events on $aws/events/presence; the N3 window still needs a scheduled check of the status table
self: native
the last will on the MQTT session; the collector marks offline when no status arrives in the window

jobs.job: identity: one credential per device, rules that spend it (chapter 7)
firebase: custom tokens minted by the Admin SDK on a server you run or a function; the rules read auth.token
aws: native
an X.509 certificate per thing with a policy on ${iot:Connection.Thing.ThingName}; fleet provisioning for the claim flow
self: add-on
a password or client certificate per client in the broker's auth plugin and an ACL per client id; a claim service you write

jobs.job: shape checks on what a device writes
aws: add-on
the rule's SQL selects fields; a Lambda action validates the rest
self: you build
the collector validates (pydantic or a schema) and drops what fails

jobs.job: OTA: a signed image the device fetches, and a per-device rollout record (chapter 9)
firebase: the image in Cloud Storage (Blaze plan) or in the database as text; the signature, the staged rollout and the state record are yours
aws: native
IoT Jobs with a signed S3 object and a rollout configuration
self: you build
an HTTPS file server, a signature the device checks, and a topic that names the version per device

jobs.job: an app that shows live values on a phone with an offline cache
firebase: the mobile SDK: listeners, local cache, reconnection
aws: add-on
MQTT over WebSockets with Cognito credentials, or AppSync subscriptions; the cache is yours
self: you build
MQTT over WebSockets from the phone to your broker, or an API you expose; the cache is yours

firebase: automated backups to Cloud Storage on the Blaze plan; restore is an import
aws: native
S3 versioning, DynamoDB point-in-time recovery, both priced per GB
self: you build
pg_dump or snapshots on a schedule, tested restores, and the disk to hold them

firebase: 200 000 simultaneous connections and one region per database instance; beyond that, shard devices across instances
aws: native
soft account limits (500 000 connections per account by default, raisable); multi-region is a second deployment
self: you build
whatever one broker and one database take before you cluster them; measure, then add nodes
